event_description: December Atmospheric River and Winter Weather Event, Emergency Assistance, and Truck Driver Hours Waiver

December Storm Damage — starting on December 3rd, 2023, Washington State experienced an unprecedented atmospheric river event, with rain causing damage to road infrastructure in Clallam, Grays Harbor, Mason, Skagit, and Snohomish Counties
July Extreme Weather and Flooding in Douglas and Grant counties

Autumn Storms — a series of severe autumn storms struck Washington state between November 3, 2022 and November 8, 2022, producing straight-line winds and heavy rainfall, resulting in flooding, saturated soils, and landslides in Clallam, Cowlitz, Grays Harbor, Island, Jefferson, Lewis, Okanogan, Pierce, Skagit, Skamania, Snohomish, and Wahkiakum counties

State of Emergency — dangerous fire fuel and weather conditions exist throughout the state of Washington, creating a high risk of severe wildfires igniting and demanding immediate response of firefighting resources to protect people, homes, businesses, and public and private property

State of Emergency — a combination of above normal snowpack in the mountains, above average temperatures, and recent rainfall has resulted in higher than normal snow melt causing flooding of rivers and streams in Ferry, Okanogan and Pend Oreille counties

State of Emergency — since June 2017, we have experienced drier than normal weather conditions with periods of above average temperatures throughout the State which, when combined with projected weather and fire fuel conditions for early September, present a high risk of severe wildfires throughout the State of Washington
State of Emergency — from Since March 10 through April 21, 2017, a series of severe storms struck Washington, producing extreme rainfall throughout the region
State of Emergency — from March 10 through March 20, 2017, a series of severe storms struck Eastern Washington, producing extreme rainfall throughout the region

State of Emergency (February Storms) — from January 30, 2017 through February 22, 2017, a series of severe winter storms struck Washington State, producing high winds, heavy snowfall, ice accumulation, and extreme rainfall resulting in major flooding, saturated soils, landslides, stream bank and slope erosion, fallen tree limbs, broken and uprooted trees, and flying debris
State of Emergency (Storm Damage) — from January 21 through January 28, 2016, a series of significant winter storms struck Western Washington producing extreme rainfall throughout the area

State of Emergency (Wind Storms) — on August 29, 2015, a severe storm producing extreme rainfall and windy conditions struck parts of western Washington, resulting in fallen tree limbs, broken and uprooted trees, and flying debris causing loss of life and extensive damage to homes, businesses, public utilities, public facilities, electrical power systems, infrastructure, and property

State of Emergency (Okanogan County mudslides) — on July 15, 2014, Proclamation 14-04 was issued proclaiming a state of emergency throughout Eastern Washington due to existing wildfires and the extreme risk of additional wildfires, including the 270,000 acre Carlton Complex wildfire in Okanogan County that continues to burn and has resulted in significant damage to homes, public facilities, and roadway infrastructure

State of Emergency (Eastern Washington) — GOVERNOR 14-04 WHEREAS, the month of July 2014 has been extremely dry, there are multiple ongoing wildfires throughout Eastern Washington, and current and projected weather conditions, in conjunction with existing and projected fire fuel conditions, present a continuing high risk of severe wildfires throughout all counties of Eastern Washington State

State of Emergency - Grays Harbor, King, Lewis, Lincoln, and Pierce counties — between March 5 and March 24, 2014, a series of severe storms occurred in Grays Harbor, King, Lewis, Lincoln, and Pierce counties, producing extreme rainfall resulting in saturated soils, erosion, and issuance of flood and landslide warnings throughout Western Washington
State of Emergency - US 12 — a series of storms producing high winds and rain occurred in parts of western and central Washington from September 28, 2013, through October 1, 2013
